item.title: New findings on how a 70-year-old leukemia drug works
item.description: A 70-year-old leukemia drug is still yielding new insights. Researchers found that removing a protein called NUDT5 protected cells from the drug.

item.title: How the brain resolves conflicting visual information
item.description: The brain may have a built-in way to quickly settle disagreements between regions processing the same scene, according to researchers.

item.title: Distant time crystals may synchronize into the same rhythm
item.description: Researchers found that multiple time crystals in a semiconductor can synchronize their oscillations, similar to pendulum clocks gradually falling into sync.

item.title: ADHD and autism diagnoses have surged; large study may explain why
item.description: A large Danish study found that children diagnosed with ADHD or autism today more closely resemble their peers in the general population than those diagnosed previously.
